description: Customer purchased a wireless keyboard (EUR 89.99) 45 days ago. Key switches are failing. Customer requests full refund. Outside 30-day return window but within 6-month warranty.
notes: Product defect is clear from photos provided.

description: Customer demands complete deletion of all personal data under GDPR Art. 17. Customer has no open orders or pending returns. Account active for 3 years.
notes: Need to verify no legal retention obligations apply.

description: Customer claims they lost EUR 50,000 in business revenue due to a 6-hour platform outage on Oct 28. Threatens litigation if not compensated. Attached letter from their attorney.
notes: Attorney letter references breach of SLA. Customer is on Business Standard plan with no SLA guarantees.

description: Customer wants to return an unopened monitor (EUR 349.00) purchased 12 days ago. No defect — simply changed their mind.
notes: Standard return, within 14-day cooling-off period. Should not require legal.

description: Customer's laptop screen has dead pixels after 4 months. Customer insists this is a manufacturing defect covered by warranty. Product team says dead pixels under 5 are 'within spec'.
notes: Customer has 3 dead pixels. Company policy says 5+ required for warranty claim, but customer cites EU consumer protection.

description: Customer was charged twice for a monthly subscription (EUR 29.99 x 2). Requests refund of the duplicate charge plus a service credit for the inconvenience.
notes: Duplicate charge confirmed in billing system. Standard correction.

description: Enterprise customer claims 3 SLA breaches in Q3 2024, totaling 14 hours of downtime against a 99.9% uptime guarantee. Demands EUR 25,000 in contractual penalties plus a 20% discount on next year's renewal.
notes: SLA logs confirm 2 of 3 claimed breaches. Third incident was scheduled maintenance with prior notice.

description: Customer received a damaged headset (EUR 149.00). Box was crushed during shipping. Requests replacement or refund.
notes: Photos confirm shipping damage. Carrier liability likely.

description: Customer requests a full copy of all personal data held by TechForward under GDPR Art. 15. Wants it in machine-readable format within 30 days.
notes: Standard DSAR. Need to coordinate with Data team for export.

description: Customer ordered express delivery (EUR 15.99 shipping) for a birthday gift. Package arrived 5 days late. Customer demands full order refund (EUR 199.99) plus EUR 50 compensation for 'ruined birthday'.
notes: Express delivery guarantee was 2 business days. Carrier tracking confirms 7 business days.

description: Customer's 8-month-old printer shows paper feed issues. Customer claims warranty, but the product was used in a commercial setting (small office) despite being sold as a consumer product.
notes: Warranty terms specify 'personal/household use only'. Customer argues they weren't informed at purchase.

description: Customer experienced 4 hours of service unavailability on Nov 1. Requests one month free subscription (EUR 29.99) as compensation.
notes: Outage confirmed. Standard consumer plan — no SLA, but goodwill gesture appropriate.

description: Customer subscribed to annual plan (EUR 299.99) 2 months ago. Wants to cancel and receive a pro-rated refund for the remaining 10 months. Terms state annual plans are non-refundable.
notes: Customer argues they should have been warned about non-refundable terms more prominently. German consumer protection may override T&C.

description: Customer reports that a USB-C charger (EUR 39.99) overheated and caused minor burn marks on their desk. No injuries. Demands replacement, desk repair costs (est. EUR 200), and assurance the product is safe.
notes: Potential product safety issue. May need to involve product safety team and consider recall implications.

description: Customer purchased software license (EUR 59.99) 10 days ago. Wants full refund — says the software doesn't work as advertised. Software was downloaded and activated.
notes: Digital content refund rules under EU Distance Selling Directive. Customer may have waived withdrawal right upon download.

description: Customer wants account and all data deleted. However, customer has an open warranty claim (CC-2024-005) and an unpaid invoice of EUR 149.00.
notes: GDPR erasure right vs. legitimate business interest for open claims and unpaid invoices.

description: Customer's 14-month-old tablet has a battery that no longer holds charge. Manufacturer warranty is 12 months. Customer argues EU law provides a 2-year guarantee for defects.
notes: Customer may be correct — EU Consumer Sales Directive provides 2-year legal guarantee. Need legal clarification on burden of proof after first year.

description: Customer was charged EUR 14.99 for an add-on service they claim they never subscribed to. Wants refund for 3 months (EUR 44.97) and assurance it won't recur.
notes: Subscription logs show customer clicked 'Start Free Trial' 3 months ago, which auto-converted. Opt-in confirmation email was sent.

description: Enterprise customer exceeded their 500-seat license by 47 seats for 2 months. Auto-billing charged EUR 4,700 in overage fees. Customer disputes, claiming they weren't notified of the overage threshold.
notes: Contract clause 7.3 specifies overage billing. Notification email was sent to IT admin, but customer claims admin left the company.

description: Customer's new wireless mouse (EUR 69.99) has intermittent Bluetooth connectivity issues. Purchased 18 days ago. Wants full refund rather than replacement.
notes: Within return window, defect confirmed. Standard refund process.

description: Customer received a data breach notification email and demands to know exactly what data was compromised. Also wants EUR 5,000 compensation for 'emotional distress' and a written guarantee it won't happen again.
notes: Minor breach affecting email addresses only. Already reported to supervisory authority. Compensation claim under GDPR Art. 82.

description: Customer dropped their laptop and cracked the screen. Claiming warranty coverage because 'the laptop should be more durable.' Product is 5 months old. Repair cost estimated at EUR 450.
notes: Physical damage from accidental drop. Clearly outside warranty scope — warranty covers manufacturing defects only.

description: Customer's cloud storage was inaccessible for 2 hours during a critical work presentation. Demands EUR 500 compensation for 'professional embarrassment' plus 6 months free service.
notes: Standard consumer plan with no SLA. 2-hour outage confirmed. Compensation request significantly exceeds subscription value.

description: Customer received the wrong color variant of a smart speaker (EUR 129.99). Wants the correct color or a full refund. Original color is now out of stock.
notes: Fulfillment error confirmed. Standard exchange/refund process.

description: Customer received notice of a 15% price increase on their business subscription (EUR 499/month → EUR 573.85/month). Customer threatens to cancel and claims they were promised 'price stability' by a sales rep at signup. No written record of this promise.
notes: Annual contract renews in 2 months. Customer on 2-year plan. T&Cs allow price adjustments with 30-day notice. Verbal promise issue.
